==English== ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|syften}}, from {{inh|en|ang|siftan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*siftijan}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/sɪft/}} * {{audio|en|En-us-sift.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪft|s=1}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[sieve]] or [[strain]] (something). # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[separate]] or [[scatter]] (things) as if by sieving. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[examine]] (something) [[carefully]]. ## {{lb|en|archaic|or|old-fashioned|transitive}} To [[scrutinize]] (someone or something) carefully so as to find the truth. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 2|I|i|23|1|As neere as I could '''ſift''' him on that argument,
On ſome apparant danger ſeene in him,
Aym‘d at your Highneſſe, no inueterate malice.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|author={{w|David Hume}}|year=1748|title=Enquiries concerning the human understanding and concerning the principles of moral|location=London|publisher=Oxford University Press|year_published=1973|section=§ 28|passage=But if we still carry on our '''sifting''' humour, and ask, ''What is the foundation of all conclusions from experience ?'' this implies a new question.}} ##* {{quote-book |en |year=1764 |author=w:Horace Walpole |title=w:The Castle of Otranto |pageurl=http://www.gutenberg.org/files/696/696-h/696-h.htm |page= |publisher=w:Strawberry Hill Press |passage=It immediately occurred to him to '''sift''' her on the subject of Isabella and Theodore.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1913|author={{w|Edgar Rice Burroughs}}|title={{w|The Return of Tarzan}}|publisher=Ballantine Books|location=New York|year_published=1963|page=108|passage=“I fear that there is something more serious than accident here, Mr. Brently,” said the captain. “I wish that you would make a personal and very careful examination of Mr. Caldwell’s effects, to ascertain if there is any clew to a motive either for suicide or murder—'''sift''' the thing to the bottom.”}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1920|author=Agatha Christie|authorlink=Agatha Christie|title={{w|The Mysterious Affair at Styles}}|publisher=Pan Books|location=London|year_published=1954|page=162|passage=Never, he said, in the course of his long experience, had he known a charge of murder rest on slighter evidence. Not only was it entirely circumstantial, but the greater part of it was practically unproved. Let them take the testimony they had heard and '''sift''' it impartially.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} {{+obj|en|:through}} To [[carefully]] go through a set of objects, or a collection of information, in order to find something. ##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2025-05-15|title=Europe’s free-speech problem|url=https://archive.is/seOtp|text=Britain’s police are especially zealous. Officers spend thousands of hours '''sifting through''' potentially offensive posts and arrest 30 people a day. Among those collared were a man who ranted about immigration on Facebook and a couple who criticised their daughter’s primary school.}} # {{lb|en|computing|dated|transitive}} To move data records up in memory to make space to insert further records. ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|outsift|presift|resift|siftability|siftable|siftage|siftproof|siftingly|sift out|sift through|sifter}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|to sieve or strain (something)|strain|purge}} * Armenian: * Aromanian: * Assamese: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Cherokee: * Chinese: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Frisian: * Friulian: * German: * Hawaiian: * Hungarian: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Latin: * Malay: * Middle English: * Norman: * Occitan: * Persian: * Piedmontese: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Rarotongan: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|просе́ивать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|просе́ять|pf}} * Spanish: * Tagalog: * Telugu: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Walloon: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to separate or scatter (things) as if by sieving|separate}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * Frisian: * German: * Italian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|отсе́ивать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|отсе́ять|pf}} * Swedish: * Telugu: * Thai: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to examine (something) carefully|judge}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * Frisian: * German: * Italian: * Latin: * Norwegian: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Telugu: * Thai: {{trans-bottom}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # An act of sifting. ====Usage notes==== * The utensil used for sifting is a ''{{l|en|sieve}}'', and not a ''sift''. ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=fist|FIST|FITs|FiTs|ITFs|TIFs|fist|fits}}
